title: Deeper fearlessness comes by tasting Naam
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 154
summary: The shabad begins with the strange claim that speaking the Unspoken becomes nectar. It carries the listener through lesser fears falling away, recognition through the Guru's Shabad, and hearts filled with the Lord's essence.
whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels harassed by many small fears. Taken seriously, it replaces scattered fear-management with a deeper orientation to the One that makes the lesser fears lose force.
takeaway: Carry this with you: taste Naam deeply enough that lesser fears stop governing you.

lines.translation: Those who speak the Unspoken, drink in the Nectar.
Other fears are forgotten, and they are absorbed into the Naam, the Name of the Lord. ||1||
Why should we fear, when fear is dispelled by the Fear of God?

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰੇ ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਪਛਾਨਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: poore gur kai sabadh pachhaanaa ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Through the Shabad, the Word of the Perfect Guru, I recognize God. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸੁ ਨਰ ਰਾਮੁ ਰਿਦੈ ਹਰਿ ਰਾਸਿ ॥ ਸਹਜਿ ਸੁਭਾਇ ਮਿਲੇ ਸਾਬਾਸਿ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: jis nar raam ridhai har raas || sahaj subhai mile saabaas ||2||
lines.translation: Those whose hearts are filled with the Lord's essence are blessed and acclaimed, and intuitively absorbed into the Lord. ||2||
Those whom the Lord puts to sleep, evening and morning
- those self-willed manmukhs are bound and gagged by Death, here and hereafter. ||3||
Those whose hearts are filled with the Lord, day and night, are perfect.
O Nanak, they merge into the Lord, and their doubts are cast away. ||4||11||

structure: First, it begins by turning what cannot be reduced to speech into nectar tasted by the heart.
Then, it lets smaller fears fall away as the Guru's Shabad reveals the Lord.
Finally, it ends in hearts filled with divine essence instead of a thousand anxious fragments.
